highlights.text: A protest petition that only objects to the police investigation cannot be treated as a complaint for taking cognizance.

highlights.caseName: State of Karnataka v. Vinay Rajashekharappa Kulkarni and Anr.
highlights.text: Suspension of ex-MLA Vinay Kulkarni's life sentence set aside in the Yogesh Gowda murder case; he goes back to jail.

highlights.caseName: Balwant Singh v. Union of India
highlights.text: Judgment reserved on Balwant Singh Rajoana's plea to commute his death sentence over delay in deciding his mercy petition.

highlights.caseName: Battula Srinu @ Mataye Kottu Srinu & Ors. v. State of Andhra Pradesh
highlights.text: CCTV footage is admissible without a Section 65B certificate when the original DVR itself is produced.

highlights.caseName: Kajal Choubey v. State of West Bengal & Ors.
highlights.text: A POSH Act Internal Committee may be headed by a man if no senior woman officer is available.

items.caseName: Deepti Singh v. State of U.P. & Anr.
items.coram: Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra, Justice Shree Chandrashekhar
items.headline: A protest petition that only attacks the police probe is not a complaint for taking cognizance
items.text: The Supreme Court said a protest petition can be treated as a complaint only if it makes specific allegations against the accused and lists witnesses. If the police investigation is defective, the Magistrate should order further investigation, and if a protest petition is treated as a complaint, the Chapter XV CrPC procedure (examining the complainant and witnesses, and an inquiry where required) must be followed before summons. The Court quashed a Banda CJM cognizance order of 25 March 2025, upheld by the Allahabad High Court, and allowed the appeal.
items.why: Sets out what Magistrates must do before summoning an accused on a protest petition after a police closure report.

items.caseName: Prabhu Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
items.coram: Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra, Justice Shree Chandrashekhar
items.headline: Acquittal in 1986 murder case where medical evidence completely contradicted eyewitnesses
items.text: Eyewitnesses said the deceased was shot in the forehead, but the post-mortem found no firearm injury, and the prosecution gave no explanation. The Supreme Court held that where eyewitness and medical evidence are completely opposed and cannot be reconciled, the case is not proved beyond reasonable doubt. It set aside the conviction upheld by the Allahabad High Court and ordered the appellant's release.
items.why: Restates when medical evidence can defeat eyewitness testimony in a murder trial.

items.caseName: State of Karnataka v. Vinay Rajashekharappa Kulkarni and Anr.
items.coram: Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra, Justice Shree Chandrashekhar
items.headline: Ex-MLA Vinay Kulkarni's life sentence revived; bail in Yogesh Goudar murder case cancelled
items.text: The Supreme Court set aside the Karnataka High Court's 31 July order that had suspended the life sentence of former Congress MLA Vinay Kulkarni and other convicts in the 2016 murder of BJP leader Yogesh Goudar, and granted them bail. Their bail bonds were cancelled and the convicts must surrender within two weeks. Their appeal against conviction will be heard by the High Court.

items.caseName: Subodh Agarwal v. State of Rajasthan
items.coram: Justice Dipankar Datta, Justice Sheel Nagu
items.headline: Bail for three former Rajasthan PHED officials in Rs 979 crore Jal Jeevan Mission tender case
items.text: The Supreme Court granted bail to Subodh Agarwal, Dinesh Goel and Mahendra Prakash Soni, setting aside Rajasthan High Court orders that had refused bail. It said further pre-trial custody served no useful purpose because the investigation is complete, the trial will be long and co-accused have been granted bail. They must appear before the trial court on fixed dates, failing which bail may be cancelled.

items.caseName: Rahul Gandhi v. S. Vignesh Shishir and Ors.
items.coram: Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Allahabad HC direction for CBI, ED to verify assets complaint against Rahul Gandhi set aside
items.text: The Supreme Court set aside the Allahabad High Court's directions asking the CBI and ED to verify a complaint alleging that Rahul Gandhi holds disproportionate assets. It sent Vignesh Shishir's petition back to the High Court to hear Gandhi afresh on all issues, including whether the petition is maintainable. Gandhi's petition and his transfer petition were disposed of.

items.caseName: Sharjeel Imam v. State of NCT of Delhi
items.coram: Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Notice to Delhi Police on Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam bail pleas; no interim bail for now
items.text: The Supreme Court issued notice to the Delhi Police on fresh bail pleas by Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid in the 2020 Delhi riots larger conspiracy case under the UAPA. It declined to consider interim bail before hearing the police. The matters will go to the Chief Justice on the administrative side for a three-judge bench, in light of the reference order in Tasleem Ahmed.

items.caseName: Balwant Singh v. Union of India
items.coram: Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Sandeep Mehta, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh
items.headline: Judgment reserved on Balwant Singh Rajoana's plea to commute death sentence
items.text: The Supreme Court reserved judgment on Balwant Singh Rajoana's plea to commute his death sentence in the Beant Singh assassination case. He argues that the delay in deciding his mercy petition, pending before the President since 2012, justifies commutation.

items.caseName: Y. Balaji v. Assistant Commissioner of Police, Central Crime Branch (Job Racketing)
items.coram: Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Trial court told to defer cash-for-jobs proceedings against ex-minister Senthil Balaji
items.text: The Supreme Court directed the trial court in the cash-for-jobs corruption case against former Tamil Nadu minister V. Senthil Balaji to adjourn the case to a date in the week starting 14 December. The State said it would take no steps in CC 24/2021 for now.

items.caseName: Yashica Bhandari Jain v. Union of India
items.coram: Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Students who already opted for CBSE's three-language option can continue
items.text: On CBSE's application to modify its 28 September order extending the third-language exemption to the current Class 6 batch, the Supreme Court clarified that students who chose three languages this academic year can continue with that choice.

items.caseName: Rupesi @ Rupesh v. State of U.P. and Another
items.coram: Justice Abdul Shahid
items.headline: Allahabad High Court upholds 25-year sentence for rape of five-year-old girl
items.text: The High Court dismissed the convict's appeal and confirmed the 25-year rigorous imprisonment imposed by the POCSO Special Court, Muzaffarnagar, for a 2013 rape. It relied on the child's testimony, corroborated by her father, uncle and the doctors who treated her. The appellant must remain in jail to complete the sentence.
items.why: Shows appellate courts will rely on a child victim's credible testimony backed by medical evidence.

items.caseName: Rajkumar Goswami v. State of U.P. and 4 Others
items.coram: Justice Arindam Sinha, Justice Satya Veer Singh
items.headline: Police officer deemed 'always on duty' can't be censured for inaction without proof of breach of duty
items.text: The Court held that Section 22 of the Police Act, 1861 cannot be used to punish an officer for failing to prevent a crime unless a specific breach of duty is shown. The Sub Inspector was not shown to be on duty at the wedding where the dispute arose. The Tribunal's judgment and the censure order were set aside.

items.caseName: Dharmendra Kumar and Another v. State Bank of India and Others
items.coram: Justice Irshad Ali
items.headline: Sale deed for UP land registered outside the State after 1994 amendment is void
items.text: After the 1994 UP amendment to the Registration Act, a Mumbai Sub-Registrar had no power to register deeds for land in Uttar Pradesh, so those deeds were void. Depositing them with a bank created no valid equitable mortgage. The Court quashed the DRT, DRAT and sale-confirmation orders and barred recovery against the plots.

items.caseName: M/s Aliganj Service Station v. Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. and Others
items.coram: Justice Irshad Ali
items.headline: Petrol pump dealership can't be ended over extra fittings when statutory seals are intact
items.text: The Court quashed the termination of a 27-year-old petrol pump dealership and the forfeiture of its deposit. The oil company had not proved the dealer installed the extra fittings, gave no personal hearing as its own guidelines require, and tested samples only after termination. The dealership was ordered to be restored.

items.caseName: Raj Kumar and Others v. Deputy Director of Consolidation, Hardoi and 5 Others
items.coram: Justice Jaspreet Singh
items.headline: Review pleas by lawyers who did not argue the original case 'not a healthy practice'
items.text: The Court dismissed a review petition in a consolidation dispute, finding no error apparent on the record. It criticised the practice of having new counsel, who had not argued the writ petition, file review pleas. The petitioners may still pursue their property claims in the proper forum.

items.caseName: Battula Srinu @ Mataye Kottu Srinu & Ors. v. State of Andhra Pradesh
items.coram: Justice K. Suresh Reddy, Justice Sumathi Jagadam
items.headline: CCTV footage admissible without Section 65B certificate if original DVR is produced
items.text: The Court held that CCTV footage was admissible without a Section 65B certificate because the original DVR was produced and marked in evidence. It upheld the murder convictions of four accused in the killing of a Sattenapalli businessman. Conspiracy convictions were set aside and one accused was acquitted.
items.why: Clarifies when electronic evidence can be proved without a certificate.

items.caseName: Kati Kesaiah & Ors. v. State of Andhra Pradesh
items.coram: Justice Y. Lakshmana Rao
items.headline: Corruption prosecution can be withdrawn with court's consent at any stage before judgment
items.text: The Court set aside Special Court orders that refused the State's request to withdraw four ACB cases against public servants under Section 321 CrPC. It held that an advanced trial stage is no bar to withdrawal before judgment. The State had chosen departmental action, which ended in punishment.

items.caseName: Shaik Fajurulla v. State of Andhra Pradesh & Anr.
items.coram: Justice Y. Lakshmana Rao
items.headline: Cheque bounce notice to director personally is not valid notice to the company
items.text: A Section 138 demand notice sent to a director in his personal capacity does not count as notice to the company. Calling him a director in the complaint cannot replace naming and serving the company. The order issuing process against the director was set aside, leaving civil remedies open.

items.caseName: Kajal Choubey v. State of West Bengal & Ors.
items.coram: Justice Reetobroto Kumar Mitra
items.headline: POSH Act committee can be headed by a man if no senior woman officer is available
items.text: The Court upheld an Internal Complaints Committee presided over by a male officer, as the POSH Act allows this when no senior woman is available. It held the 90-day inquiry timeline is directory, not mandatory. The petitioner, who took full part in the inquiry, could not now object, and the writ petition was dismissed.

items.caseName: Gnanananda Samanta v. State of West Bengal and Ors.
items.coram: Justice Saugata Bhattacharya
items.headline: Calcutta High Court seeks police report on alleged assault of TMC councillor in Bishnupur
items.text: Calling the allegations serious, the Court directed the local Inspector-in-Charge to file a report on the alleged assault of a councillor in front of police, including any arrests made. It ordered protection for the petitioner and his family if needed. The matter is listed on 6 January 2027.

items.caseName: Smt. Khushbu Kumari v. State of Chhattisgarh
items.coram: Justice Naresh Kumar Chandravanshi
items.headline: Police need prior magistrate permission to probe non-cognizable offences; later nod can't cure it
items.text: Police had completed key investigation steps before the Children's Court permitted the probe into non-cognizable offences. The Court held that Section 174 BNSS requires permission first and later approval cannot cure the illegality. The charge-sheet was quashed and the applicant discharged.

items.caseName: Gurvinder Singh v. Balvinder Singh
items.coram: Justice Naresh Kumar Chandravanshi
items.headline: Cheque bounce presumption can be rebutted on circumstances; acquittal over lost cheque upheld
items.text: The Court upheld an acquittal under Section 138 of the NI Act. The accused had told his bank earlier that the cheque book was lost, and the complainant's account had contradictions, so the presumption was rebutted. The revision was dismissed.

items.caseName: Paardarshita Public Welfare Foundation v. Union of India
items.coram: Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre, Justice Sanjay Sharma
items.headline: Delhi High Court refuses to interfere with closure of Kartarpur corridor
items.text: The Bench declined to entertain a plea to reopen the Kartarpur Sahib corridor, closed since May 2025 after the Pahalgam attack. It said the closure is a policy decision taken in the national interest. The petition was disposed of with the hope that the pending representation would be considered.

items.caseName: Megha Joshi v. Union of India & Anr.
items.coram: Justice Amit Mahajan
items.headline: Public interest must be shown to get UPSC civil services answer sheets under RTI
items.text: The Court dismissed a 2022 UPSC candidate's plea for copies and inspection of her answer books. Her worry about mark-recording errors, based on a roll-number slip affecting other candidates, showed only personal interest. Disclosure needs a larger public interest.

items.caseName: Nayabuddin v. Parveen Singh
items.coram: Justice Harish Vaidyanathan Shankar
items.headline: Landlord's death after eviction order does not by itself wipe out the decided claim
items.text: The Court dismissed a tenant's revision and upheld the eviction of a shop under the Delhi Rent Control Act. Later events matter only if they substantially displace the original need. The landlady's daughter, brought on record as legal heir, inherits the benefit of the order.

items.caseName: Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited & Ors. v. Mrinal Kanti Bhattacharjee
items.coram: Chief Justice Ashutosh Kumar, Justice Kaushik Goswami
items.headline: Courts can't replace departmental assessment of an employee without finding arbitrariness
items.text: The Court set aside a CAT order directing BSNL to ignore a retired employee's APAR gradings and grant retrospective upgradation from 2014. The Tribunal had substituted its own view without finding arbitrariness or illegality. Qualifying service or juniors' promotion alone gave no right to upgradation.

items.caseName: Bilal Ahmad Dar v. Zia ud Din Changal
items.coram: Justice Shahzad Azeem
items.headline: Security cheque can attract Section 138 if the underlying debt is unpaid
items.text: The Court refused to quash three cheque bounce complaints. A cheque given as security can still attract Section 138 of the NI Act if the liability is unpaid when it matures. Whether the cheques were only security is a defence to be tested at trial.

items.caseName: Sanatan Hembram and Others v. Hite Lal Hembrom and Others
items.coram: Chief Justice M. S. Sonak, Justice Rajesh Shankar
items.headline: Party relying on Santhal custom excluding daughters from inheritance must prove it
items.text: The Division Bench held that a Santhal custom barring daughters from inheriting must be proved to exist and continue. It declined to treat the single-judge ruling in Karan Murmu as authoritative and preferred Narayan Soren. A second appeal pending since 2006 was dismissed.
items.why: Affects inheritance rights of tribal women in Jharkhand.

items.caseName: High Court of Karnataka v. State of Karnataka
items.coram: Justice Anu Sivaraman, Justice K.S. Bharath Kumar
items.headline: Karnataka High Court seeks timeline for filling public prosecutor vacancies
items.text: In a 2019 suo motu case, the Court asked the Home Department to report steps to fill vacant prosecutor posts and give a recruitment timeline. The Home Secretary must file an affidavit. Only 157 regular appointments have been made against 411 sanctioned posts.

items.caseName: Smt. Uma Rao v. State
items.coram: Justice V. Srishananda
items.headline: Teacher taking only invited students to a private housewarming is not untouchability
items.text: The Court quashed an FIR under Section 3(1)(r) of the SC/ST Act against a retired teacher. She had attended a private housewarming with students the host invited, leaving out others. The host's choice of guests did not amount to caste discrimination.

items.caseName: Dr. Pradeep Krishna R.V. & Others v. Dr. Sunil Shenvi & Another
items.coram: Justice M. Nagaprasanna
items.headline: Doctor authorised at one hospital can do emergency transplant at another registered hospital
items.text: A doctor authorised to perform liver transplants at one registered hospital committed no offence under the Transplantation of Human Organs Act by doing an emergency transplant at another. The Court relied on a Bombay High Court ruling and noted a settlement. The criminal case was quashed.

items.caseName: Dr. Lokesh v. State of Karnataka & Anr.
items.coram: Justice H.P. Sandesh
items.headline: No quashing for government doctor accused of helping 14 Bangladeshis get Aadhaar
items.text: The Court refused to quash the case against a government doctor who allegedly attested address certificates without documents. His defence and objections on sanction must be tested at trial. In a connected petition, proceedings against another accused were quashed for lack of material.

items.caseName: Pinarayi Vijayan v. Adv. K.M. Shajahan and Ors.
items.coram: Justice Devan Ramachandran, Justice Syam Kumar V.M.
items.headline: CMRL-Exalogic case: stay on probe against ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan and kin extended till 15 December
items.text: The Division Bench extended its 26 October interim order stopping further investigation in the CMRL-Exalogic case against Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter Veena T. and Muhammed Riyas. It asked the State whether any preliminary enquiry was under way. The appeals are listed on 15 December 2026.

items.caseName: S. v. N. and Anr.
items.coram: Justice C. Jayachandran
items.headline: Husband's duty to maintain wife and child comes before repaying mother's housing loan
items.text: The Court said a husband's duty to his wife and daughter is paramount over payments on a housing loan taken by his mother. It reduced interim maintenance to Rs 7,500 for the wife and Rs 5,000 for the child. The Family Court will decide the wife's income on evidence and expedite the case.

items.caseName: The Project Director, National Highway Authority of India v. Abdul Salam B.A. and Others
items.coram: Chief Justice Soumen Sen, Justice Syam Kumar V.M.
items.headline: Arbitrator can't discard highest-valued sale deed while fixing land compensation
items.text: The Court dismissed three NHAI appeals over Kasaragod land taken for highway widening. The District Collector, acting as arbitrator, rejected the top sale deed without reasons, against Section 26 of the 2013 Act. The District Judge's order setting aside the award was upheld.

items.caseName: Usha v. Geetha (Died)
items.caseNo: C.M. Appl. No. 1 of 2026 in R.P. No. 1053 of 2026 in R.S.A. No. 716 of 2010
items.coram: Justice C.S. Dias
items.headline: Fraud allegation alone is not sufficient cause to condone 2,450-day delay
items.text: The Court refused to condone a 2,450-day delay in seeking review of a judgment upholding a decree. An allegation that the decree was obtained by fraud does not by itself show sufficient cause. Earlier liberty to file a review did not mean the delay would be excused.

items.caseName: Arun Anirudhan v. State of Kerala and Others
items.coram: Justice Devan Ramachandran, Justice Johnson John
items.headline: Elected member facing pending FIR can't force inclusion in temple advisory committee
items.text: The Court held that the Travancore Devaswom Board cannot be compelled to include a member facing criminal cases while its bye-laws require a certificate of non-involvement. It did not examine the charges themselves. He may seek re-inclusion if exonerated.

items.caseName: A v. K
items.coram: Justice G.S. Ahluwalia, Justice Anuradha Shukla
items.headline: Husband who agreed to live apart from parents can't later blame wife for cruelty
items.text: The husband had accepted his wife's conditions, including living separately from his parents, and brought her back. The Court held he had condoned the alleged cruelty and could not rely on it for divorce. The Family Court's dismissal of his petition was upheld.

items.caseName: LKB v. SB
items.coram: Justice Anand Pathak, Justice Ramkumar Choubey
items.headline: Husband can't seek divorce for desertion within a year of his own restitution decree
items.text: The Court dismissed a husband's appeal seeking divorce on desertion, cruelty and adultery. Desertion could not be claimed before one year passed after his restitution decree, and the other grounds lacked proof. His right to seek divorce under Section 13(1A)(ii) HMA was kept open.

items.caseName: MP Board of Secondary Education v. Jayendra Kumar Labana
items.coram: Justice Subodh Abhyankar, Justice Jai Kumar Pillai
items.headline: Board should print time limit for corrections as footnote on marksheets
items.text: The Court dismissed the Board's appeal against an order to correct a wrong photograph on a student's marksheet, sought six years after issue. A citizen should not suffer for an error made by a college and a State department. It suggested the Board print the correction deadline on marksheets.

items.caseName: Anushri v. The Secretary, Travancore Devaswom Board & Ors.
items.coram: Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari, Justice G. Arul Murugan
items.headline: Madras High Court declines PIL seeking Sabarimala access for transgender devotees
items.text: The Bench said the PIL was not maintainable before it because the temple is in Kerala and a similar case is pending before the Kerala High Court. The petitioner withdrew the plea. The Court did not grant liberty to approach the Kerala High Court.

items.caseName: The Branch Manager v. N Pitchaimani and Another
items.coram: Justice P Murugan
items.headline: Workman's death from work pressure covered by Employees' Compensation Act
items.text: The Court upheld an order directing the insurer to pay Rs 3 lakh to the family of a textile mill helper who collapsed and died from stress and heavy work. Death caused by work pressure during employment falls under Section 3(1) of the Act. The lack of an external injury did not defeat the claim.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.coram: Justice Pankaj Jain
items.headline: State must protect religious properties, not 'usurp' them on pretext of better use
items.text: On a petition by devotees of a dera in Sunam tehsil, the Court held the State cannot claim a religious institution's land without acquiring it and paying compensation. The managing committee had no power to transfer the dera's land. A 1994 Gram Sabha resolution and the mutation in the State's favour were quashed.

items.caseName: Sri Venkata Ramana Lorry Transport v. The Telangana State Warehousing Corporation & Others
items.coram: Justice Nagesh Bheemapaka
items.headline: State bodies can't invoke public interest to deny payment for services already used
items.text: The Court allowed a transport contractor's plea against FCI, which had withheld about Rs 91 lakh. Having approved the rates and let the work go on for years, FCI could not refuse payment citing public interest or lack of privity. The dues were ordered to be released with interest.

items.court: Additional District and Sessions Court, Taliparamba, Kerala
items.caseName: The Station House Officer v. T.P. Biju and Others
items.coram: Judge K.N. Prasanth
items.headline: Three BJP-RSS workers get life sentence for 2016 murder of CPI(M)'s C.V. Dhanaraj
items.text: A day after convicting them, the court sentenced T.P. Biju, M. Vipin and M. Vaishakh to life imprisonment and fined each Rs 5 lakh, to go to Dhanaraj's heirs. It held the case did not meet the rarest of rare test for death. Sixteen other accused had already been acquitted.
